sections.content:
13,710 people

were counted on the census as "telephone salespersons" in England and Wales in March 2021.
Telephone salespersons obtain, receive, process and record telephone orders for goods and services.

People who had this job were generally younger

The occupation of "telephone salespersons" had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

The largest age group of people who had this job were those aged 20 to 24 years. Of the whole working population 7.9% were aged 20 to 24 years. For people working as "telephone salespersons", 19.6% were in this age group.

The age group with the smallest proportion of people working as "telephone salespersons" was 65 years or older.

sections.content:
Other jobs that had a similar age profile to "telephone salespersons" included:

  • elementary construction occupations (other)
  • sports coaches, instructors and officials
  • customer service occupations (other)

Select your age group to see the ten most popular occupations for your age

A similar number of men and women had this job

Among people working as "telephone salespersons" there were a similar number of men and women (46.1% compared with 53.9%).

This means "telephone salespersons" had a similar proportion of men and women compared with the wider occupation group it falls within of "sales occupations".

Men made up 46.1% and women made up 53.9% of "telephone salespersons"
Across the whole working population, 52% were men and 48% were women. This occupation was one of the jobs for which the proportion of men and women was closest to this overall picture.

Other jobs that had a similar proportion of men and women to "telephone salespersons" included:

  • generalist medical practitioners
  • leisure and theme park attendants
  • buyers and procurement officers

These are the occupations for which the proportion of men and women was most equally split:

  • quality assurance and regulatory professionals
  • chartered and certified accountants
  • conservation professionals

We can look at who worked as "telephone salespersons" by age group and for men and women at the same time to see how these two factors interact.

Men and women with this occupation had a similar age profile, as shown in the chart below.

The percentage of men and women who are "telephone salespersons" across age groups

How many people do this job by disability status, employment type and area

Of people working as "telephone salespersons", 11.6% were disabled. This means people said they had a long-term condition that limited them "a little" or "a lot" in their day-to-day activities. The average for all occupations is 9.6%.

Disability is more common among people who are older. This occupation had a younger age profile compared with the whole working population.

People with this job were more likely to work full-time than part-time (72.9% compared with 27.1%).

They are also more likely to be an employee (93.5%) than self-employed (6.5%).

The region of England and Wales with the highest percentage of people with this job was the North West. At a local level, the areas with the highest percentage of people in this occupation included Kingston upon Hull, City of, this is in the region of the Yorkshire & Humberside.
